sources.entry: Middleclick - Emulate a scroll wheel click with three finger Click or Tap on MacBook trackpad and Magic Mouse

summary.one_liner: MiddleClick is a macOS utility that turns a three-finger click or tap on a MacBook trackpad or Magic Mouse into a middle mouse (scroll wheel) click.
summary.what_it_does: The app runs in the macOS menu bar and emulates a middle click when three fingers click or tap on a MacBook trackpad or Magic Mouse. Per the README, the middle click works system-wide, such as closing a browser tab by middle-clicking it, opening a Safari link in a background tab, and pasting selected text in Terminal. The finger count is configurable through a defaults setting (for example 4, 5, 2, or up to 10), and an option allows extra fingers to still trigger the click. Tap sensitivity is tunable via maximum distance and maximum time deltas. The README notes support for macOS Sequoia 15. The README also states the project is finished and that its successor, WheelClick, provides the same three-finger click and tap behavior.
use_cases: middle-click on a trackpad without a mouse
close browser tabs with a three-finger tap
open Safari links in background tabs
paste in Terminal with a trackpad gesture
emulate scroll wheel click on Magic Mouse
customize finger count for middle click
how_to_run: Building from source: clone the repo, run make, and find MiddleClick.app in ./build/ (requires Command Line Tools)
stack: Swift/Objective-C (macOS app, inferred from build with make and Command Line Tools)
notable: Three-finger click and tap emulate a middle mouse button on trackpad and Magic Mouse
Finger count is configurable, including 2 to 10 fingers
Tap distance and timing thresholds are tunable through defaults keys
Development is finished; the successor WheelClick is described as the continuation of this functionality
caveats: The README states MiddleClick is finished and no longer actively developed
Setting fingers to 2 conflicts with normal two-finger right-click and single-finger clicks
Accessibility permission issues after updates and possible Three Finger Drag conflicts are listed in troubleshooting
Antivirus tools such as CleanMyMac may flag it as a false positive
